blocks.x: Permit processing on governed agents, median cycle time down 41% and completeness problems resolved before submission, not after
Identity withheld, a city government whose building-permit queue was measured in months and whose applicants measured it in frustration. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter timed the queue: 71-day median permit cycle, 38% of applications returned once for completeness, adding six weeks per return, and planners reviewing files that lacked the documents the checklist already demanded.
The checklist existed; enforcement of it was manual and polite. Each return cycle restarted the clock, and the applicant's experience was the restarting.

We moved permits to governed agents: submissions checked against the codified checklist at intake with missing items and likely errors surfaced immediately, completeness conversations happening before formal submission where the applicant portal allows, file assembly automated for the planner with every requirement mapped to its document, and the checklist versioned under the building office. Planners review buildings, not paper.
